midi.role: normal mode: incoming notes go to the Part chosen with PART SELECT
midi.note: CORRECTION 2026-09-23 (from the OCR'd owner's manual): the MC-303 has no single settable MIDI channel, so the home channel 12 assigned earlier cannot be set. In normal mode it plays incoming MIDI on ANY channel into the Part selected with PART SELECT (effectively omni). In Sound Module mode each Part has a fixed receive channel (see MIDI Implementation). It TRANSMITS Parts 1-7 on channels 1-7 and the Rhythm Part on channel 10 (fixed). Practical rule: give it its own MIDI line, and don't merge its MIDI OUT into the RD-9/Digitakt chain. Channel 12 is free again. Accepted by the owner 2026-09-23.

midi.role: fixed: drum voices on ch 10, bass synth on ch 1
midi.note: No settable channel. Akai's official MIDI implementation page (Akai Japan, dated 2014-12-24; archived copy at https://web.archive.org/web/20170729082239/http://www.akai-pro.jp:80/rhythm-wolf/data/midi.php, saved as sources/akai-rhythm-wolf-midi-implementation.pdf) lists fixed channels: KICK 36, SNARE 38, PERC 40, HH OPEN 42, HH CLOSE 44 on ch 10; BASS SYNTH note 36 on ch 1; velocities 0/42/84/127. So it CANNOT take home channel 15 (released). Its drums collide with the RD-9 (10) and its bass with the K2 (1): give it its own MIDI line, never the RD-9/Digitakt/Thru5 chain.

recording-session.notes: Recording session in the main studio. The RD-9 is the master clock (gear-kb). Add swapped-in synths from the palette: their MIDI cables from the Thru5 are patched automatically.

settings.notes: Logic Pro (recording sessions, per gear-kb inventory).
Normally connected to the Mac Mini M4 (Logic Pro). Ports not named.
Port name is the owner's wording ('main out'); the Digitakt manual is not ingested to check it.
OUT, not THRU: the Thru5 gets the Digitakt's own clock/transport (following the RD-9) plus its MIDI tracks. The RD-9's ch 10 notes stop at the Digitakt.
THRU forwards the RD-9's stream unchanged (clock, transport, ch 10 notes), so the Analog Four is clocked by the RD-9 one hop earlier than the Thru5 synths.
Owner 2026-09-23: reaches Logic Pro on the Mac Mini over the UMC1820's existing USB link. One Thru5 output is still free.

open_statements: The RD-9 is the master clock.

The Mac receives MIDI through the UMC1820 MIDI IN (fed by a Thru5 output, i.e. the Digitakt's MIDI OUT stream). Nothing sends MIDI from the Mac to the gear. Replaces the 2026-09-20 statement 'Nothing sends MIDI back to the Mac.'
Default UMC1820 inputs: 1 RD-9, 2 open, 3/4 Analog Four, 5/6 Eurorack, 7/8 Digitakt. Everything runs straight into the interface; main outs are used on everything, with TS or TRS cables as needed.
Gear not in that default list (for example the Korg M1, Dreadbox Typhon, Behringer K2, Donner B1) is swapped in and out as needed. Where its audio goes when in use is not yet stated.

Swap rule: gear swapped in takes the UMC1820 input(s) of the gear it replaces. MIDI does not follow the slot: each instrument keeps its own home channel (midi_channels.yaml), and the trigger source is re-pointed instead.
The Analog Four's CV OUTPUTS A-D are sometimes used as CV tracks into the Eurorack. Which module inputs is not yet stated.

CV / gate / trig sources into the Eurorack: Analog Four MKII, Korg SQ-64, Arturia KeyStep (original), and the Behringer K2 (any of its outs). Each goes into 'various module inputs'; which module inputs is not yet stated.
